claims.answer: Terminal-only client (interactive TUI, print and JSON modes) on macOS, Linux, native Windows (Git Bash/PowerShell) and WSL, plus Termux; programmatic RPC and SDK; no desktop GUI app, mobile app, browser UI or editor extension in the repository.

desktop_os.answer: Runs on macOS, Linux (ARM64 and x86-64 via Nix) and Windows natively or in WSL; it is a terminal program, not a desktop GUI.

mobile_apps.answer: No mobile app in the pinned monorepo or documentation; Termux is a terminal environment.

browser.answer: No browser client; session export produces HTML only.

cli.answer: pi launcher with interactive, print, JSON and RPC modes.

task_actions.answer: Start, steer (Enter), queue (Alt+Enter), stop (Escape) and resume sessions in the terminal.

notifications.answer: An example notify extension exists but no built-in notification channel.

cross_device_continuity.answer: Sessions are local files; continuing elsewhere requires the same session file or /share exports.

limitations: No GUI, web or phone client; IDEs integrate through RPC/SDK that third parties build.

claims.answer: Pi embeds its own agent loop (pi-agent-core) and talks to many model providers directly; it does not host other coding harnesses in the release (a pi-claude-code provider repo exists separately); extensions can add providers and tools.

limitations: Only the Pi harness runs in the product; other CLIs are not controlled.

claims.answer: Bring-your-own API keys for many providers, OAuth subscription logins for supported providers (Anthropic, GitHub Copilot, OpenAI Codex legacy, Kimi) and local models (llama.cpp docs, custom providers); no Pi vendor credits.

evidence.title: Pi README
evidence.locator: Sections intro, Getting started, Packages, Permissions & Containerization
evidence.finding: Pi is a minimal extensible agent harness; skips sub-agents and plan mode; interactive, print/JSON, RPC and SDK modes; installs via curl/PowerShell/npm/Nix; no built-in permission system; requires Node.js 22.19+.

evidence.title: Use Pi in the terminal
evidence.locator: Enter a prompt; Change direction; Continue or start over; Run a terminal command
evidence.finding: Terminal transcript and editor; Enter steers a running task, Alt+Enter queues a follow-up, Escape stops; sessions auto-saved, /resume, /tree, /fork, /compact, /export; footer shows context usage and accumulated cost.

evidence.title: Pi quickstart
evidence.finding: Install, run pi in a folder, /login to use a subscription, API key or a local model.

evidence.title: Providers
evidence.finding: /login supports OAuth or API keys; many providers (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google Gemini, GitHub Copilot, Mistral, Groq, xAI, OpenRouter, Bedrock, Vertex and more); credentials stored in auth.json.

evidence.title: pi-ai README
evidence.finding: Lists API-key providers and OAuth providers including OpenAI Codex (ChatGPT Plus/Pro, legacy), GitHub Copilot and Kimi For Coding subscription endpoint.

evidence.title: MCP servers
evidence.finding: Pi is an MCP client for stdio and streamable HTTP servers with pi mcp add/list, /mcp, user and project config and bearer/OAuth auth; project config needs project trust.

evidence.title: Run Pi safely
evidence.locator: Choose how to run Pi; Understand project trust
evidence.finding: Pi does not ask approval before every tool call and has no security boundary; project trust gates loading of .pi resources; sandboxing is by running Pi in container, VM or sandbox.

evidence.title: Run Pi in an isolated environment
evidence.finding: Plain Docker, Docker Sandboxes, OpenShell and the Gondolin micro-VM extension are documented isolation methods; credentials handling differs.

evidence.title: RPC mode
evidence.locator: Start RPC mode; Protocol records; Reference
evidence.finding: pi --mode rpc runs Pi as a subprocess with JSONL commands, responses and events for IDEs and custom UIs; extension UI forwarding.

evidence.title: SDK
evidence.locator: Session lifecycle; Prompting; Subscribing to events
evidence.finding: TypeScript SDK embeds Pi sessions in Node.js or Bun with prompting, events and session configuration.

evidence.title: Sessions and context
evidence.locator: Continue or switch sessions; Choose how to branch; Manage conversation context; Export or share a session
evidence.finding: Saved sessions with /resume, /tree, /fork, /clone, compaction, /export HTML/JSONL and /share upload.

evidence.title: Settings
evidence.finding: Retry settings (3 retries, exponential backoff); enableInstallTelemetry default true; enableAnalytics default false.

evidence.title: Environment variables
evidence.finding: PI_TELEMETRY overrides install/update telemetry and attribution headers; PI_OFFLINE disables automatic network activity.

evidence.title: Packages
evidence.locator: Install and manage packages; Create a package
evidence.finding: Pi packages bundle extensions, skills, prompt templates and themes installed from npm, git or paths with project or user scope.

evidence.title: Extensions
evidence.locator: Examples table (subagent/, plan-mode/, ssh.ts, git-checkpoint, permission-gate, notify, todo)
evidence.finding: Extensions register tools, commands, UI and hooks; the examples directory ships optional example extensions for sub-agents, plan mode, SSH, permission gates, git checkpoints and todos that are not enabled by default.

evidence.title: Skills
evidence.finding: Pi loads agent skills, AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md context files and prompt templates.

evidence.title: Choose a model
evidence.finding: Models are selected with /model; custom and local providers (llama.cpp docs) can be configured through models.json.

evidence.title: Run Pi on Windows
evidence.finding: Native Windows (Git Bash or PowerShell tool) or WSL are supported; README also documents Termux and Nix for Linux/macOS.

evidence.title: Compaction
evidence.finding: Conversation history is compacted manually or automatically near the context limit.

evidence.title: Command line
evidence.finding: Interactive, print (-p), JSON and RPC modes; --continue, --session-dir, --no-session, --offline.

evidence.title: pi-durable README
evidence.locator: Intro; Persist and Resume; Abort and Subagents
evidence.finding: Experimental durable agent harness runtime committing conversations and tool calls to storage so a dead process resumes; API changes without notice.

evidence.title: pi-claude-code repository
evidence.finding: Community-style provider in the earendil-works organization to access a Claude Code subscription via claude-code in Pi.

evidence.title: pi-chat repository
evidence.finding: Separate Apache-2.0 repository for Slack/chat automation and workflows with Pi.

evidence.title: Gondolin repository
evidence.finding: Experimental Linux micro-VM sandbox with a TypeScript control plane (Apache-2.0), used by the Gondolin extension to isolate built-in tools.

evidence.finding: Release v1.5.0 published 2026-11-02T11:05:31Z.

evidence.finding: Public monorepo: 122,328 stars on 2026-11-16, MIT license (GitHub API spdx MIT), pushed 2026-11-16.

evidence.title: pi.dev homepage
evidence.finding: Product homepage: minimal agent harness, install commands, links to documentation, changelog, models, packages and Radius; shows no paid Pi plan on the homepage.

evidence.title: Pi LICENSE

evidence.title: coding-agent package.json
evidence.finding: Package @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent version 1.5.0, license MIT, bin pi.

evidence.title: Auth storage
evidence.finding: Credential storage for API keys and OAuth tokens per provider with refresh flows (anthropic, openai-codex, github-copilot providers).

evidence.title: MCP server loader
evidence.finding: Implements MCP client loading of user and project servers.

evidence.title: Session manager
evidence.finding: Session persistence as JSONL entries with parent IDs enabling tree branching, compaction entries and export.

evidence.finding: Install/update telemetry reporting gated by enableInstallTelemetry and PI_TELEMETRY.

evidence.title: Bounded source search of the pinned release
evidence.locator: Paths packages/coding-agent/src, packages/agent/src, packages/coding-agent/docs; terms: worktree, issue tracker, kanban, backlog, pull request, createPullRequest, cron, scheduler, multiplayer, collaborat, co-prompt, rbac, sso, saml, organization role, subagent, plan mode, webhook
evidence.finding: No built-in worktree management, issue tracker, kanban, pull request integration, scheduler, multi-user collaboration, roles or SSO exists in core; matches are the footer showing a git worktree name, cache warming, documentation of examples (subagent, plan-mode) and unrelated identifiers.

evidence.title: Subagent example extension source
evidence.locator: index.ts lines 46-66 (usage stats), 263-320 (onUpdate streaming, spawn args --mode json -p --no-session), 453-465 (agentScope, confirmProjectAgents)
evidence.finding: Example extension spawns separate pi processes with --mode json -p --no-session, streams partial results through onUpdate, reports per-agent turns, tokens, cost and context, preserves full output in tool details, and asks confirmation before running project-local agents.

evidence.title: Subagent example README
evidence.finding: Each subagent runs in a separate pi process with streaming output, parallel streaming, usage tracking and abort propagation; project-local agents are off by default and need confirmation in untrusted projects.

evidence.title: coding-agent CHANGELOG
evidence.finding: Per-release changelog records removals of deprecated APIs and model IDs (for example deprecated minimax model IDs) and release dates; no product-level deprecation or end-of-life notice for Pi itself.

evidence.title: pi-durable README (replay semantics)
evidence.locator: Tools section: replay safe, interrupted, restart_limit
evidence.finding: In the durable runtime a tool call interrupted by a crash reruns on reopen only when declared replay: safe; otherwise the model receives an interrupted error result with output committed so far; repeated restarts end in restart_limit.

evidence.title: SSH example extension
evidence.finding: Optional example extension routing tools to a remote host over SSH; not enabled by default.

evidence.title: pi-chat ConversationRuntime
evidence.locator: formatTranscriptRecord (line 45 uid and userName per inbound record); isAllowedInput (lines 129-138, allowedUserIds and allowedRoleIds); shouldQueueTrigger and job_queued records (lines 174-236)
evidence.finding: The optional pi-chat extension (separate repository, last commit 2026-06-05) bridges Discord and Telegram channels to one sandboxed pi session; inbound messages from different users are logged with their user ID and name, access can be restricted to listed user or role IDs, and channel mentions or DMs queue jobs for the agent.

changes.author: agent:ADE-84
changes.summary: Independent review: the official pi-chat extension (separate earendil-works repository) lets several people in one Discord or Telegram channel drive the same pi session with per-user attribution and user/role allowlists, so TEAM-01 was not 'single-user with no co-prompting' and the multiplayer 'no' mapping is removed; COORD-04 events now names the chat-triggered job queue.

before.answer: Single-user local sessions; /share uploads a session as a viewer link (read-only sharing); no presence or co-prompting.

after.answer: The pi CLI is single-user and /share uploads a read-only viewer link; the optional pi-chat extension from the same organization (separate repository, not in the v1.5.0 monorepo, last commit 2026-06-05) lets several people in one Discord or Telegram channel send messages to the same pi session with per-user attribution and user or role allowlists; no presence indicators or conflict handling are documented.
